source.title: Solutions to two open problems in topological residuated lattices

accepted.question_text: Let L be a BL-algebra, or more generally a residuated lattice, with a linear topology U. Choose a base beta for U such that every basic open set containing the top element 1 is a filter of L. Let X be the subfamily of beta consisting of the basic open sets that contain 1, let Y be all finite intersections of members of X, and write Y = {F_i : i in I}. Order I by i <= j exactly when F_j is a subset of F_i, so that Y is an upward directed system of filters. This system induces another topology V on L whose basic neighborhoods are of the form x/F_i for x in L and F_i in Y. What necessary and sufficient conditions ensure that V is finer than U, and hence that U and V coincide?
accepted.context_brief: Filter-induced topology on a linear topological BL-algebra or residuated lattice

evidence.quote: the problem of finding suitable condition such that \mathcal{V}$\mathcal{V}$ is finer than \mathcal{U}$\mathcal{U}$ is still open.

accepted.question_text: Let L be a residuated lattice and let F(L) be the set of all filters of L. For each filter F, define T_F = {U subseteq L : for every x in U, x/F is contained in U}; this construction makes (L, T_F) a linear Alexandrov topological residuated lattice, and distinct filters produce distinct topologies, so there is an injective map from F(L) to LTRL(L), where LTRL(L) denotes the set of all linear topological residuated lattices whose underlying set is L. Are the sets F(L) and LTRL(L) equipotent?
accepted.context_brief: Cardinality of filter topologies versus linear topological residuated lattices

evidence.quote: whether the sets $\mathcal{F}(L)$ and $LTRL(L)$ are equipotent?
